record.original_question: For functions on a finite interval, can one characterize all one-parameter families of fractional derivatives that are associated with the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals through the first fundamental theorem of fractional calculus, meaning that each derivative family acts as a left inverse of the corresponding Riemann-Liouville fractional integral on the relevant function space?

evidence.quote: According to the property HL3) from the desiderata, a fractional derivative for the functions defined on a finite interval is introduced as a linear operator Dalpha, alpha >= 0 left inverse to the Riemann-Liouville fractional integral Ialpha, i.e., as an operator that satisfies the relation (1st Fundamental Theorem of FC) (Dalpha Ialpha phi)(x) = phi(x), x in [0, 1] (11) on appropriate nontrivial space of functions.

Characterize all families of the fractional derivatives for the functions defined on a finite interval that are associated to the Riemann-Liouville fractional integrals through the 1st Fundamental Theorem of FC (the nth level fractional derivatives including the Riemann-Liouville, Caputo, and Hilfer derivatives are examples of such families).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\alpha\ge 0$ and let $I^\alpha$ denote the Riemann–Liouville fractional integral on the finite interval $[0,1]$, defined for $\alpha>0$ by
$$(I^\alpha \varphi)(x)=\frac{1}{\Gamma(\alpha)}\int_0^x (x-t)^{\alpha-1}\varphi(t)\,dt,\qquad x\in[0,1],$$
and $I^0=\mathrm{Id}$. A one-parameter family $\{D^\alpha\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ of linear operators, each acting on a suitable nontrivial space of functions on $[0,1]$, is called a family of fractional derivatives associated with the Riemann–Liouville fractional integrals through the first fundamental theorem of fractional calculus if for every $\alpha\ge 0$ the operator $D^\alpha$ is a left inverse of $I^\alpha$, i.e.
$$(D^\alpha I^\alpha \varphi)(x)=\varphi(x),\qquad x\in[0,1],$$
on the chosen function space.

Known examples of such families include the Riemann–Liouville fractional derivatives, the Caputo fractional derivatives, the Hilfer fractional derivatives, and the so-called $n$th level fractional derivatives.

Problem: Provide a complete characterization (classification) of all one-parameter families $\{D^\alpha\}_{\alpha\ge 0}$ of fractional derivatives on $[0,1]$ that are associated with the Riemann–Liouville fractional integrals through the first fundamental theorem of fractional calculus in the sense above.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature (e.g. work by Luchko and follow-ups through 2023–2024) introduces broader generic fractional derivatives left-inverse to the Riemann–Liouville integral and shows infinitely many such families exist beyond Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Hilfer, and the nth-level derivatives, but a complete classification remains unresolved; related sub-questions (e.g., existence of such derivatives with infinite-dimensional null space, or with finite-dimensional null spaces different from the nth level derivatives) are explicitly listed as open problems.

status_evidence.title: On a Generic Fractional Derivative Associated with the Riemann–Liouville Fractional Integral
status_evidence.snippet: Infinitely many other families of fractional derivatives that are left-inverse operators to the Riemann–Liouville fractional integrals exist; focus on an important class and their properties.
status_evidence.claim: Full characterization is not yet achieved; new families continue to be constructed.

status_evidence.title: The General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives on a Finite Interval
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses fractional integrals and derivatives on finite intervals satisfying fundamental theorems of fractional calculus.
status_evidence.claim: Problem remains an active topic with ongoing developments.

status_evidence.title: Fractional derivatives and the fundamental theorem of fractional calculus
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces nth level fractional derivatives as further examples of left inverses of Riemann–Liouville integral and lists open problems on classifying such derivatives.
status_evidence.claim: Classification stated as an open problem.
